newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly lower in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly lower in quiet trade.

text.p: After a session of choppy trading, soymeal futures ended near session lows Tuesday, under pressure from late commission house sales, floor traders said.
Griffin Trading was the largest late seller in the soymeal pit, but volume was light through the session, traders said.
Soyoil futures ended mixed, but January soyoil futures found some support from commercial stopping of deliveries, traders said.
Term Commodities stopped 2,008 of 3,092 contracts delivered against Janury on Tuesday, first notice day, according to CBOT data. There were no soymeal deliveries.
Final stocks data from the U.S. Census Bureau put soyoil stocks at 1.896 million pounds. That figure was within trade expectations and considered neutral for futures, floor traders said.
Trade was quiet in both product markets ahead of the New Year's holiday on Wednesday when the CBOT will be closed.
Soyoil settled up 0.10 to down 0.04 cent per pound, with January steady at 22.71. Soymeal futures closed down $2.20 to $0.30, with January down $2.20 at $226.30.
Talk that China was seeking up to 300,000 tonnes of soymeal from Brazil and India helped underpin that market, floor traders said.
On the day, ADM Investor Services bought 300 lots soymeal, Continental Grain bought 150 lots and Smith Barney bought 200 January. Cargill sold 100 lots January and 200 March.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 contracts, below the 26,468 traded Monday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, below the 20,139 contracts traded Monday.
